name: Gillette India Ltd
title: Gillette India Ltd - 507815 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: FY26 sales up 8% to ₹3,100 crore and PAT up 23% to ~₹650 crore, but management admits near-term challenges and gives no numeric FY27 guidance; supply-side signals are thin.

summary.headline: Gillette India FY26 sales rose 8% to ₹3,100 crore and PAT rose 23% to about ₹650 crore, with the company citing a ~300bps structural margin gain.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) sales of about ₹3,100 crore, up 8%, and PAT of about ₹650 crore, up 23%, attributed to productivity across cost buckets. Management said the topline slowdown was largely due to one-time export impacts from affiliate distribution changes, including the Bangladesh distribution agreement closure, and that domestic sales were growing quarter on quarter. The call focused on new launches (Gillette Guard 3in1, Gillette trimmers, Oral-B Sensitive), Venus growth, productivity, and raw material inflation linked to the West Asia conflict. Management gave no numerical FY27 guidance.

segments.name: Male grooming (Blades and Razors)
segments.commentary: Management says the category grows about 12% and Gillette remains market leader; male grooming offtake grew 8% in P6M and 12% in P12M. Gillette Guard grew double digit and premium razors grew in early teens.

segments.name: Female grooming (Venus)
segments.commentary: Venus contributes double digits to grooming and is growing upwards of 20%; female grooming overall is growing upwards of 20%. The focus is new-user growth in in-home hair removal.

segments.name: Manual oral care (Oral-B)
segments.commentary: Growing high single digits, driven by the Oral-B Sensitive range, which is growing double digit and is among the fastest growing segments in the category.

segments.name: Power oral care (Oral-B)
segments.commentary: Growing at roughly 1.5x this year and at double digits steadily; business has doubled in the last 3 years.

segments.name: Trimmers and appliances
segments.commentary: Four new Gillette trimmers launched about 2 months before the call; management expects the trimmers category to grow at early double digits.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 sales or margin guidance was given; management said it expects some challenges to continue in the near term.
Management aims to grow ahead of the male grooming category and keep balancing topline and bottom-line growth.
A multi-year savings and productivity plan is in place by business unit to support margins and offset input-cost inflation.
Management said it cannot comment on future margins but expects productivity to fund investment and provide cover against macro volatility.
Management expects growth may fluctuate in the mid-term; it sees India growing at 6.5% for the year.
capex_capacity: About 85% of products are manufactured domestically; finished goods are exported to more than 10 countries.
Bhiwadi manufacturing plant issue was resolved within a few days with zero supply-related shortfall, per management.
Management is constantly assessing the locally manufactured vs imported supply chain mix.
Supply 3.0 advance ordering now covers half of the business; over 2 million automated on-shelf availability checks are run daily.
demand_pricing: Gillette Guard 3in1 (launched about 2 months earlier): about 1 million razors sold in the launch month, distribution reached over 6 lakh stores, and a new copy reached 20 crore viewers in month 1.
Numeric distribution rose by a couple of points in FY26 for priority SKUs; premium Mach3 and Fusion distribution grew at mid-single digits for 3 years.
Gillette Guard added 20 million new users over the last 3 years.
Management said raw material costs were hit by crude up ~50% and resins up ~50%, with availability challenged; the company said it did not go out of stock.
Management said rural consumption remains higher than urban, but rural is softening because of inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue growth subdued and volatile in FY26 and the March quarter, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-time export impacts from affiliate-company decisions, including the Bangladesh distribution agreement closure, weigh on the base. Excluding them, growth would roughly double, and domestic sales are growing quarter on quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY26 margin gains sustainable, and what about FY27 margins and raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said structural margins improved upwards of 300 bps through premium innovation and productivity. It would not comment on FY27 but said a multi-year savings plan is in place and it will keep mitigating inflation and freight overcharges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth plan over the next 3 to 5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will double down on its five-vector integrated strategy: daily-use portfolio, superiority, productivity, constructive disruption and an enabled organisation. No numeric target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth drivers in Venus and female grooming?
qa_highlights.answer: Venus is double digit in grooming and growing upwards of 20%; the focus is new-user growth in in-home hair removal through influencers and myth-busting content. No Venus salience figure was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trimmers and appliances opportunity, and what share is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Four trimmers were launched about 2 months before the call; the category is expected to grow at early double digits. Management aims to grow faster than the category but gave no share target.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Bhiwadi plant issue fully resolved, and were there supply challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the issue was resolved within a few days, with zero supply-related challenges, and the stock exchange was alerted.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: crude and resin up about 50%, with tight availability tied to West Asia conflict; the margin impact was not quantified.
Export revenue volatility from affiliate distribution changes, including the Bangladesh agreement closure.
Softening rural consumption and inflation-driven pressure on consumer spending.
Competition in men's shaving, which management acknowledged in Q&A without giving share data.
Next quarter: whether domestic growth and margin gains hold, and the early traction of Guard 3in1 and trimmers.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term record and category growth, but cautious on near-term challenges from inflation and supply costs. It deflected several quantitative questions (FY27 margins, share targets, Venus salience, the innovation pipeline) and said some information would be withheld as price sensitive.
key_quotes: We have consistently grown topline AND bottom-line for the last 5 years!
Gillette continues to be the market leader in the Blades and Razors segment, and we have grown year on year.
As an example, crude has been highly volatile and prices have gone up by 50%. As an outcome, resins have gone up by about 50% as well.
Despite these significant disruptions, we have not gone out of stock… or made compromises on product performance.

growth.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was given; management expects "some challenges to continue," with growth backed only by launches (Gillette Guard 3in1, four new trimmers), Venus and productivity savings of ₹38 crore, with no capacity additions or order book cited.
